guard: a wait for the delivery daemon we launched is not answered by some OTHER daemon's ready lease (#837)
why: THE READY FLAG ANSWERS A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED. `ready:true` on the shard-0 lease means SOME
daemon bound `ctl.delivery`; the caller is asking whether THE DAEMON IT JUST STARTED did. Those
differ exactly when it matters: a SIGKILLed holder leaves its ready record for the rest of the
bucket TTL, so a replacement that lost the CAS and exited was reported ready off the corpse's
lease. The mutation restores that read, and the assertion it must redden is the one that names
a DIFFERENT holder - not the control that waits for the real one, which stays green under it.
THE TWO CONTROLS ARE PART OF THE PROOF, not decoration. Scoping the wait to a holder can fail in
the other direction - answering false for a daemon that IS ready, or refusing the ADOPTION case
where the caller genuinely cannot know the id of a daemon that was already running. Both are
asserted beside the negative, so a fix that simply never returns true does not pass this suite.
NO BUILD STEP BELONGS HERE. The suite imports `../src/index.js` relatively, so the mutated file
IS the module under test. A `completionMarker` IS declared: this suite is not fail-fast (it
counts pass/fail and prints its banner either way), so a run that dies before the banner died of
something other than the assertion named.

mutations.name: the wait accepts ANY ready lease again, as it did before #837
mutations.find: if (info.ready === true && (opts.holder === undefined || info.holder === opts.holder)) return true;
mutations.expectRed: a ready lease held by another daemon does NOT answer for the one we launched

mutations.name: a rearm that fails part-way records itself as SERVING, so the retry is lost
mutations.expectRed: Q4 and the endpoint is STILL QUIESCED after that failure, not silently un-quiesced
mutations.note: Found in review, and the recovery path re-introducing #1318's own class. armPlane3 binds in four stages, so it can throw with some bound. Leaving the flag lowered on that throw records the endpoint as serving while it is not: every later rearmPlane3 returns at the !plane3Quiesced guard WITHOUT retrying, and resumeServing then flips the lease READY over missing bindings. A transient broker error becomes a permanent readiness lie. Q5 and Q6 grade the lost retry and Q8 reads the durable back off the broker, so this is graded by broker state rather than only by the flag it mutates.

mutations.name: M3 the launcher derives the lease holder as the bare connection nkey
mutations.expectRed: the holder a launcher derives from the cred alone MATCHES the row the daemon wrote
mutations.cell: the holder a launcher derives from the cred alone MATCHES the row the daemon wrote
mutations.note: The shipped defect, restored. `idFromCreds` is the daemon's identity at the CONNECTION layer and reads as the obvious answer, but the endpoint rewrites card.id to the principal dot-form before stamping it into the row, so a launcher comparing against the bare nkey can never match. It fails in the safe direction - the fresh-launch readiness wait simply times out and reports a ready daemon as not-ready - which is exactly why it survived: a guarantee defeated by a comparison that never fires looks like a slow start rather than a bug. The refusing control beside the cell (a DIFFERENT cred must not match) stays green under this mutation, so the kill is attributable to the derivation rather than to the comparison collapsing.
